label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
To: kitbash-market/murmur-dialogue/reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: 4 stars - Lanternfolk wouldn't exist without it, but read this before buying 3.2

I've used Murmur since 2022, since v1.3, so I think I'm one of the oldest users here. I want to give a balanced picture, because the page right now is mostly people being angry, and some of it is fair and some of it really isn't.

First the honest part, because if you're thinking about buying it you need to know this:

**3.2.0 has a save bug.** If you load a save that was made with 3.1.x, every Murmur variable goes back to its default value. In our game that means the ferryman forgets you already paid him, quest flags reset, that kind of thing. It looks like the save key changed from node path to uid in 3.2, but that's my guess, I haven't dug into the code properly. Either way it's real, other people have confirmed it, and it won't be fixed by the original dev.

**The fix is to roll back to 3.1.4.** That works for us and for others in the forum thread. Old saves load fine again.
1. Back up your project first (seriously).
2. Get the 3.1.4 release.
3. Replace the Murmur folder in your project's addons folder with the 3.1.4 version.
4. Keep a copy of 3.1.4 somewhere safe and don't update to 3.2.

That's what we're doing for our launch. We have 412 dialogue nodes and 9 languages through Murmur's CSV export, and everything runs fine on 3.1.4.

**There is no support anymore.** Ines posted on 30 Oct that 3.2 is the last version she'll make. So if you buy it now you're buying it as it is. No bug fixes, no Godot updates from her. That's why I give 4 stars and not 5. If you need something with active support for a big commercial project, take that seriously.

Now the other part.

The first prototype of our game Lanternfolk was the ferryman scene. I made it in one weekend in 2022 with Murmur, and it was the first time something I made felt like an actual game and not just a test. That weekend is basically why I quit my job at a mobile studio and started doing this full time. So when I say Lanternfolk wouldn't exist without this plugin, I'm not exaggerating.

As a tool it's still the nicest dialogue system I've used in Godot. The node editor is clear, conditions and variables just work, barks and voice line hooks are easy to set up, and the CSV localisation export saved us so much time with 9 languages. It never felt like a hobby project, even though it was one person.

About the "took our money and ran" stuff: I paid 19 dollars in 2022 and got four years of updates for that. One person maintained this for four years. She shipped an update with a bug, then she told everyone clearly that she was stepping back, apologised for the bug, and put the whole source on the public repo under MIT so anyone can fork it. That is the opposite of running. You can be annoyed about 3.2, I was too when I found the bug, but some of the reviews here are just cruel and I don't think that's okay to write about a person.

Also, because it's MIT now, this doesn't have to be the end. Someone can fork it and fix the save issue properly. I might look at it myself after our launch, no promises, but if someone else starts a fork first I'd be happy to help test.

**Short version for new buyers:**
- Great tool, especially for branching dialogue and localisation
- Use 3.1.4, avoid 3.2.0 until a fork fixes the save bug
- No official support anymore, buy it knowing that
- Source is MIT, so you're not locked in

And Ines, if you ever read this: thank you. Really. For four years of work and for a tool that changed what I do with my life. I hope you're doing okay.

- Jonna, Stugaspel
